title: Indices, Logarithm and Surds Quiz 7
description: Same-base equations, one step at a time.
instructions: Indices, Logarithm and Surds: Exponential equations.
Write maths answers with the keypad. Any equal form is accepted.
Every question has a trap. Slow down at the signs.

questions.question: Solve $5^{3x}=5^{7x-2}$.
questions.explanation: Equal bases, so the indices are equal: $3x=7x-2$, which gives $x=\dfrac12$. Watch out: $3x-7x=-2$ gives $-4x=-2$, so $x$ is positive.

questions.question: Solve $4^{t^{2}}=4^{6-t}$. Give all the solutions.
questions.explanation: Equal bases: $t^2=6-t$, so $t^2+t-6=0$ and $(t-2)(t+3)=0$. Watch out: there are two solutions, $2$ and $-3$.

questions.question: Solve $3^{z}=9^{z+5}$.
questions.explanation: $9^{z+5}=3^{2z+10}$, so $z=2z+10$ and $z=-10$. Watch out: $9=3^2$, so the index $z+5$ doubles.

questions.question: Solve $4^{5-9x}=\dfrac{1}{8^{x-2}}$.
questions.explanation: With base $2$: $2^{10-18x}=2^{-3x+6}$, so $10-18x=-3x+6$ and $x=\dfrac{4}{15}$. Watch out: $\dfrac1{8^{x-2}}=2^{-3(x-2)}$, with the minus sign on the whole bracket.

questions.question: What is the best first step to solve $2^{x}=7$?
options: Cancel the base from both sides
questions.explanation: $7$ is not a power of $2$, so we take a logarithm: $x\ln2=\ln7$. Watch out: $2^x$ is not $2\times x$, so dividing by $2$ does nothing.

questions.question: If $b^{x}=b^{y}$ then $x=y$ for every positive base $b$.
questions.explanation: The base must also be different from $1$: $1^{3}=1^{5}$ but $3\neq5$. Watch out: $b=1$ breaks the rule.

questions.question: Solve $9^{x}=27$ as a decimal.
questions.explanation: $3^{2x}=3^{3}$, so $2x=3$ and $x=1.5$. Watch out: $9=3^2$, so the index is $2x$, not $x$.

questions.question: Solve $2^{2x+1}=32$. One step is wrong. Tap it.
questions.explanation: From $2x+1=5$ we get $2x=4$, so $x=2$. Watch out: subtract $1$ from both sides, do not add it.

questions.question: Write $\dfrac{1}{8^{x-2}}$ as a power of $2$.
questions.explanation: $8=2^3$, so $8^{x-2}=2^{3x-6}$ and the reciprocal is $2^{-(3x-6)}=2^{-3x+6}$. Watch out: the minus sign applies to the whole bracket.

questions.question: Which equations can be solved by writing both sides with the **same base**?
questions.explanation: The first three have bases that are powers of one base ($4$, or $3$ and $9=3^2$). $7^x=9$ and $2^{4y+1}=3^y$ need logarithms. Watch out: $7$ and $9$ share no base.
